sec/01_abstract_intro.tex.text: We present ( emonstration d stillation for ample- fficient mitation earning), which takes the flag as given and decides the other two: it partitions a round's failures into modes over a geometric descriptor and prescribes the configuration of a demonstration not yet collected, checked for feasibility before any expert time is spent.

The failures of a round are not independent events but a small set with structure, and that structure is recoverable from geometry: a descriptor of the configuration at the step where the policy first becomes unreliable partitions them into geometrically distinct groups.

An expert demonstration is the one input to imitation learning whose cost does not fall when compute is bought or a simulator is downloaded, so under a fixed allowance the only lever left on policy performance is what each demonstration contains.

[t] The query-efficient members of the DAgger family gate the expert behind a per-state predicate on action discrepancy [c], predictive uncertainty from dropout [c] or an ensemble [c], novelty and risk [c], or a diffusion policy's own per-step denoising loss [c].

Performance scales with the coverage of a policy's demonstrations, while those added within a covered region saturate [c], so once an allowance of $X$ demonstrations is fixed, the content of each is all that is left to choose (Figure~ ).

We evaluate on five tasks under two observation modalities, ten task-modality settings in all, at a budget of twenty demonstrations, against the query-efficient DAgger family and a uniform-random allocation control.

sec/02_related.tex.text: The five compared here differ only in the score: a classifier predicting deviation from the expert [c], the concentration of dropout samples about the expert's action [c], the variance of a policy ensemble combined with an action discrepancy [c], a novelty term and a task-risk estimate [c], and the per-step denoising loss of a diffusion policy [c], which Diff-DAgger reads as an uncertainty signal

Active learning ranks candidates by an acquisition function [c], through uncertainty [c] or coverage, which core-set solves by a greedy $X$-centre rule [c] and which BADGE reaches by k-means++ over gradient embeddings [c]; sub-trajectory retrieval ranks segments of a demonstration corpus [c].

Dataset aggregation corrects the covariate shift of behaviour cloning [c] by labelling the learner's own visited states and refitting on the aggregate, trading a bound quadratic in the horizon for a linear one [c], a skeleton every method compared here shares.

The remaining machinery is standard and is not claimed: the clustering, the cluster count, the diversity rule and the grid path checker are named with their sources in the Method, at the point each is used.

The graph makes such a request checkable, holding workspace bounds, spawn ranges, reachability, controller limits, the success predicate and the failure-mode vocabulary as structured knowledge, in the manner of a robot knowledge base [c] rather than a retrieval index over text [c].

The policy class is fixed by the modality and shared by every arm: an MLP on GridWorld (state), a CNN on GridWorld (image), and a diffusion policy [c] on the four robot tasks, with an R3M encoder [c] on the image branch.

A high pre-retrain loss admits two readings, novel data or an incoherent demonstration, and the second is excluded by construction: an infeasible configuration never reaches the expert (Eq.~ ), and the demonstration comes from the expert whose trajectories are the fitting target.

The baseline to be beaten moves between rows: Diff-DAgger on Push-T, Wipe and Door under both modalities, ThriftyDAgger on GridWorld (state), Stagger on GridWorld (image), a tie with ThriftyDAgger on Lift (state), and three baselines level at 99.6 on Lift (image).

What carries the result is the recurrence of the margin across the rows rather than the size of any one of them: the seed standard errors overlap in several rows, and no row would support the claim on its own.

On GridWorld (image) the random control finishes level with every gate, at 89.1 against 88.4 to 88.8, so the gate signal buys nothing there while DISEIL still gains 2.2 points, which is consistent with the ablation that follows.
